## Exercise 6.1: Build it — a minimap {#ex-6.1}

A second camera, zoomed out to fit the whole map, that never follows anyone:

```js
const miniWidth = 200;
const zoom = miniWidth / map.widthInPixels; // <1>
const miniHeight = Math.round(map.heightInPixels * zoom);
this.minimap = this.cameras
  .add(this.scale.width - miniWidth - 16, 16, miniWidth, miniHeight) // <2>
  .setZoom(zoom)
  .setBackgroundColor(0x0f172a)
  .centerOn(map.widthInPixels / 2, map.heightInPixels / 2); // <3>
this.minimap.ignore(this.label); // <4>
```
1. 200 pixels of screen for 1280 pixels of map is a zoom of about 0.16.
2. `cameras.add(x, y, width, height)` makes a camera that draws into that rectangle of the screen. It sees the same world as the main camera.
3. Point it at the middle of the map. It doesn't follow, so it stays there.
4. Every camera draws every game object unless told otherwise. Without this line the "Stored" label appears, tiny, in the minimap too.

{{< game solutions/06/ex-6.1 caption="A minimap from a second camera." >}}

The full file is in `solutions/06/ex-6.1/`. Cameras are cheap to add and very flexible: split screen, picture-in-picture, a zoomed-in "security camera" on the freezer are all a few lines each.

## Exercise 6.2: Predict it — no bounds {#ex-6.2}

In the **corner**, the camera keeps the researcher centred, so three-quarters of the screen shows the empty space beyond the map: the game's background colour, dark blue-grey. In the **middle** of the map, nothing changes, because the bounds only matter near the edges.

`setBounds` is the difference between "a camera that follows the player" and "a camera that follows the player and never shows the void". With bounds, the researcher walks off-centre near edges, which is what you expect from almost every 2D game.

## Exercise 6.3: Spot the bug — the invisible lab {#ex-6.3}

The first argument to `addTilesetImage` is the tileset's name **inside the map**, which is `lab`. The second is the key of the image you loaded, `lab-tiles`. They passed the image key twice.

With the wrong name, `addTilesetImage` can't find the tileset, logs a warning and returns `null`. Phaser still makes the layers, but they have no tileset to draw from, so they're invisible, and no tile has the `collides` property, so nothing is solid.

```js
const tiles = map.addTilesetImage('lab', 'lab-tiles');
```

The warning even tells you the right name: `Its tilesets are [...]` lists the tilesets the map really has. To see a tileset's name, open the map in Tiled and look at the **Tilesets** panel, or search the `.tmj` file for `"name"` inside `"tilesets"`.

## Exercise 6.4: Tune it — the camera {#ex-6.4}

- **Lerp 1**: the camera is glued to the researcher. Precise, but every small movement shakes the whole world, which can feel jittery.
- **Lerp 0.12**: a slight ease. The researcher leads the camera a little, and stops feel soft. This is what *Cold Chain* uses.
- **Lerp 0.02**: the camera lags so far behind that the researcher can walk off screen before it catches up. Disorienting, and dangerous with carts about.
- **Deadzone 200 × 120**: the camera only moves when the researcher leaves a box in the middle. Calm, but you can't see far ahead in the direction you're walking.

A top-down game where danger comes from every side wants the player near the centre. A side-scrolling platformer usually wants a wide, short deadzone (the camera doesn't bob with every jump) and often a **look-ahead**: an offset in the direction of movement, so you can see what you're running towards (`cam.setFollowOffset(-100, 0)` when moving right).

## Exercise 6.5: Build it in Tiled — your own floor {#ex-6.5}

There's no single answer. The steps that trip people up:

1. **Save the copy next to the tileset image**, or fix the image path. The map stores the tileset image as a path relative to the map (`../tiles/lab.png`). Saving in `public/assets/maps/` keeps that path working.
2. **Give new objects a Class.** A point with no class is ignored by `all('cart')`.
3. **Add both cart properties**, `axis` (string: `x` or `y`) and `speed` (a number). A missing `speed` makes `prop(c, 'speed')` return `undefined`, and `addCart` falls back to its default of 100.
4. **Load the new key**: `this.load.tilemapTiledJSON('my-floor', 'maps/my-floor.tmj')` and `this.make.tilemap({ key: 'my-floor' })`.
5. **Hard refresh** the browser (`Shift` + reload) if your changes don't appear: browsers sometimes cache JSON files.

If a bench you added doesn't block you, check it's on the `walls` layer, not `decor`.
